summary: Preserve original throw completion precedence when IteratorClose itself fails.

target.notes: The return getter/call is attempted as specified, but the original throw completion wins over errors from return lookup/call/result validation.

caveats: This differs from naively wrapping disposal in a C# finally whose exception can replace the original exception.

tests.name: body throw wins over return throw
tests.input: const it={next(){return {value:1,done:false}},return(){throw "close"},[Symbol.iterator](){return this}}; try{for(const x of it){throw "body"}}catch(e){console.log(e)}

tests.name: break lets return throw escape
tests.input: const it={next(){return {value:1,done:false}},return(){throw "close"},[Symbol.iterator](){return this}}; try{for(const x of it){break}}catch(e){console.log(e)}
